text:
omar: seeing a regression on TP all-reduce latency after the kernel-selector change. small messages (~8KB) p99 jumped ~2.4x on our 8xA100 cluster. any ideas?
jen: when did the selector change land? which flag?
omar: merged yesterday afternoon — default kernel profile now prefers 'vectorized-kernel-v2' for compute-bound shards. i think it affects packing/fragmentation.
kevin: can you paste the bench command and env?
omar: bench cmd: `./run_tp_allreduce --shards 8 --msg-size 8192 --iters 200 --batching auto`
env dump: `REDFW_KERNEL_SELECTOR=auto
REDFW_BATCH_COALESCE=on
NCCL_ALGO=auto
NCCL_BUFFSIZE=16777216`
omar: perf-bot run attached shows the delta.
perf-bot: run 2026-03-17T08:12:01Z — bench=tp_allreduce_smallmsgs — baseline(past-week): p99=1.8ms, p50=0.42ms; current(commit=abc123): p99=4.3ms (+139%), p50=0.48ms (+14%). throughput drop ~18%. message-size histogram: 1-4KB (12%), 4-16KB (68%), 16-64KB (20%).
sophie: interesting that p50 barely moved but p99 doubled — sounds like tail queuing/fragmentation/regression in rendezvous/warmup path. did you see more NCCL retries?
omar: i checked logs, we see repeated "rendezvous delayed" entries around allreduce start for smaller fragments. also more CPU-side serialization in profiler.
jen: can you run with NCCL_ALGO=tree and NCCL_ALGO=ring toggled? might expose ring vs tree sensitivity.
omar: ran both quickly: `NCCL_ALGO=ring` -> p99 4.1ms, `NCCL_ALGO=tree` -> p99 2.0ms. so tree seems better for these msg sizes.
kevin: that suggests the kernel selector's vectorized-kernel-v2 path is producing message fragmentation that favors tree. maybe new kernels emit different chunk sizes which interact badly with ring handshake.
sophie: also check KV cache interaction — if prefix caching reduces local compute, the shape of comm windows changes and can produce more small-window allreduce calls. are you seeing more small kv-cache hits?
omar: yes, after the model-run profile, prefix cache hits increased ~22% and avg sequence-length dropped, so more smaller allreduce windows.
jen: put up a quick flame: CPU wait stacks show threads stuck in `cudaMemcpyAsync` + `ncclComm` for extra 1-2ms before compute. that's the tail.
infra-bot: cluster telemetry: 8xA100, driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.x, NCCL 2.18.3. background network jitter minimal.
kevin: rules of thumb — ring is bandwidth-optimal for large contiguous transfers, tree can lower latency for many small reductions. the handshake/fragmentation threshold matters. where does kernel selector set chunk_size?
omar: selector sets chunk_size = min(4096, max(1024, seq_len/8)) for v2 path — so for 8KB messages it chooses 1KB chunks which creates ~8 fragments.
sophie: 8 fragments -> ring has 8x handshake overhead. tree can aggregate earlier. consider increasing chunk_size threshold or enabling coalescing at comm layer.
jen: try `REDFW_BATCH_COALESCE=aggressive` and bump kernel selector threshold to prefer >4KB chunks. also test `NCCL_BUFFSIZE=4194304` to force different rendezvous sizing.
omar: tried `REDFW_BATCH_COALESCE=aggressive` + chunk_size floor 4096 -> p99 2.1ms, throughput back to baseline. with `NCCL_BUFFSIZE=4194304` i see small improvement too but less than coalesce.
kevin: ok this points at two interacting causes: (1) kernel-selector produced smaller chunking for v2 kernels, and (2) default NCCL ring handshake costs amplify tail when fragmentation count increases.
sophie: long-term fix options: (A) update kernel selector heuristics to factor expected NCCL handshake cost and prefer larger chunking for TP allreduce sizes, (B) implement comm-side micro-coalescing to merge small fragments before issuing NCCL ops, (C) add a fallback policy: if p99 climbs for a workload shape, force NCCL_ALGO=tree for that model/route.
omar: i can prototyping (A) and (B). quick patch to selector to multiply chunk_size by 2 for TP workloads reduces tail.
jen: add a regression-test: bench harness should include small-msg envelope (1-16KB) and assert p99 within x% of baseline after selector changes.
perf-bot: created perf-regression alert ticket #PR-4521 referencing bench run 2026-03-17T08:12 and baseline 2026-03-10.
kevin: also check kernel codegen: v2 might change memory access pattern causing extra memcpy; a microbenchmark of compute-only vs comm-only would help isolate.
omar: agreed — i'll run compute-only v2 vs v1 microbench and send logs.
sophie: thanks — if you get reproducible patch, we can roll canary with `force-ncc l=tree` for the model route while we ship selector fix. :thumbsup:
omar: i'll follow up with a short PR and attach bench logs. thanks all.
jen: nice triage. small note: document findings in runtime/selector/notes so oncall can flip the fallback quickly if we see customer impact.
omar: will do.
